title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts ranks 11th in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States, down from 9th in 2025.
The state excelled in healthcare, ranking second, but fell short in fiscal stability (39th) and infrastructure (38th).
Education dropped to 7th place in 2026, contributing to Massachusetts' overall decline in the Best States rankings.

title: Massachusetts loses two IHOP restaurants
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IHOP closed locations in Cambridge at 16 Eliot St. and Hyannis at 790 Iyannough Rd.
Approximately 19 IHOP franchise locations remain open across Massachusetts after the closures.
Dine Brands Global, owner of IHOP, plans to add 245 franchisees in the next seven years.

title: Court agrees Wu did not discriminate against North End restaurants, but may have illegally taxed them
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: U.S. First Circuit Court of Appeals upheld dismissal of discrimination claims by North End restaurants against Boston Mayor Michelle Wu.
The court rejected claims of anti-Italian discrimination in outdoor dining policy, focusing on legitimate quality-of-life concerns.
The appeals court allowed the possibility of challenging the legality of the 2022 impact fees as an unlawful tax.

title: MassDOT releases rendering of two new bridges along McGrath Highway
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MassDOT plans two new bridges on McGrath Highway: Squires Bridge and Somerville Avenue Extension Bridge.
Squires Bridge will be a 300-foot beam bridge with separated bike lanes and sidewalks, replacing a deteriorated structure.
Somerville Avenue Extension Bridge relocates a hazardous road, aiming to improve driver safety and neighborhood connectivity.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ review: Peter Parker grows up in emotionally mature sequel
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: Tom Holland returns as Peter Parker in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' portraying a more emotionally mature character.
Set in a perpetually gray New York City, Spider-Man faces an internal struggle and a faceless, body-hopping villain.
Zendaya's performance shines as MJ, showcasing a broader range and chemistry with Holland in the latest Spider-Man film.

title: This Boston law firm is boosting starting salaries to $235,000
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: McDermott Will & Schulte LLP raised starting salaries for first-year associates to $235,000 effective July 1, 2026.
The salary increase aims to align with top national firms amid competition for legal talent, matching New York's Milbank.
Boston's major firms, like Ropes & Gray, have not announced similar salary increases as of July 2026.

title: Boston will host the second-ever National Urban Rat Summit
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston will host the second National Urban Rat Summit on September 23-24, announced by Mayor Michelle Wu.
The Boston Rodent Action Plan emphasizes integrated pest management, reducing reliance on rodenticides, and promoting sanitation and trapping.
A six-year study by Tufts University found rats in Boston carry leptospirosis, highlighting the need for proactive pest management.

title: Mass. postal worker robbed at gunpoint
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A USPS worker in Billerica was robbed at gunpoint for an arrow key on Thursday.
The suspects, two men in a black Cadillac, fled toward Chelmsford Street after the robbery.
Billerica Police are investigating; arrow keys provide access to mailboxes and locked mail receptacles.

title: Myrtle the sea turtle weighs nearly 500 pounds. What does it take to keep her healthy?
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Myrtle, a green sea turtle at New England Aquarium, weighs 488 pounds and receives quarterly health check-ups.
Veterinary staff at the aquarium conduct full exams, checking turtle flippers, shells, and using ultrasounds for health monitoring.
Aquarium’s annual exams of resident sea turtles aid broader conservation efforts for endangered and threatened sea turtles.

title: New program aims to bring electric vehicles to Mass. communities
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: The CommunityEV Carshare pilot will introduce solar-powered EV charging stations in Boston, Chelsea, Framingham, and Quincy.
The program, backed by a $1 million grant, aims to provide affordable EV access in underserved communities.
Eligible users can rent shared EVs at discounted rates, with no additional cost for charging at designated stations.
